en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to safely keep premature babies warm in rural Philippine hospitals without reliable electricity.
National hero Jose Rizal studied ophthalmology in Europe to learn eye surgery which he later used to cure his mother’s cataracts.
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology issues earthquake warnings so citizens can safely evacuate before disasters strike.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces with stone-walled canals that safely channel water and prevent soil erosion during heavy rains.
The Executive Branch’s Department of Health enforces the National Immunization Program to protect all Filipino children from preventable diseases like measles.
Under the Philippine Constitution every citizen has the right to health which includes the government's duty to provide clean drinking water.
National Scientist Dr. Alfredo Santos isolated active chemicals from native lagundi plants to create scientifically proven herbal medicines for coughs.
The Ecological Solid Waste Management Act requires barangays to segregate trash preventing clogged drains that breed dengue-carrying mosquitoes.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is practically applied during typhoons when neighbors work together to safely evacuate vulnerable families.
During the Pahiyas Festival locals use natural achiote seeds to dye rice flakes demonstrating the safe use of natural food coloring.
The Office of Civil Defense trains Filipino citizens in practical first aid fire safety and disaster preparedness to save lives.
Learning local health terms like lagnat for fever helps Filipino children accurately describe physical symptoms to doctors for correct medical treatment.
